filename: Equatorial Pacific pCO2 Interannual Variability in CMIP6 Models.pdf
title: Equatorial Pacific pCO2 Interannual Variability in CMIP6 Models
code_availability: Information on installing and using the CMIP6 data pre-processing Python package (Busecke & Abernathey, 2020) can be accessed here: https://cmip6-preprocessing.readthedocs.io/en/latest/
testbed_rationale: This study performs a diagnostic model evaluation of CMIP6 models and observational products using Reynolds decomposition, EOF, and correlation analyses; it does not train, benchmark, or provide machine learning parameterizations or emulators.
pain_points: Most CMIP6 models systematically underestimate interannual variability of surface ocean pCO2 and air-sea CO2 flux, while overestimating sea surface temperature variability.
Mean vertical gradients of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) are biased weak across CMIP6 models compared to GLODAPv2 observations, damping the non-thermal response to upwelling.
Thermal and non-thermal pCO2 anomalies excessively cancel each other in models, resulting in unrealistically weak net pCO2 anomalies.
extraction_notes: The research was supported in part by the NSF LEAP Science and Technology Center (STC 2019625). Although some observational products in SeaFlux rely on machine learning algorithms (such as SOM-FFN or neural networks), the study itself does not develop or apply machine learning methods.
